severities.P0: App cannot load, mission cannot complete, hidden-truth leak, data corruption, or official result mismatch.
severities.P1: Serious incorrect behavior, major scientific misrepresentation, major accessibility blocker, or reproducibility failure.
severities.P2: Significant workflow, usability, teaching, benchmark, or performance gap.

categories.SCI: Scientific model, assumption, evidence, unit, or validation concern.
categories.EDU: Teaching, onboarding, explanation, terminology, or misconception concern.
categories.BENCH: Benchmark artifact, fairness, notebook, solver packet, import/export, reproducibility, timing, or result-parity concern.
categories.UX: User interaction, navigation, discoverability, layout, or workflow friction.
categories.OPS: Pilot operations, feedback intake, checklist, release, or support process.
categories.PERF: Rendering, boot, frame timing, memory, or resource lifecycle.
categories.ACCESS: Keyboard, focus, contrast, semantics, reduced motion, or screen-reader issue.

items.title: Environment Studio domain, resolution, tile bathymetry, editable terrain
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Authoring
items.summary: Alpha testers want a unified editor for defining spatial domain size, resolution, bathymetry generation, regional bathymetry tiles, editable or deformed terrain, and import/export.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-STUDIO-R0 architecture and contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment-authoring requirements are tracked without adding a fifth Product Hub pillar.
Contracts remain separate from simulation, scoring, and scientific-model changes.
Future visible editor work can reference one stable feedback item.

items.title: Researcher Notebook Launchpad from inside ANCHOR
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / External Solver Evaluation / Researcher Quick Start
items.summary: Alpha testers are unsure whether they must download the full source project and upload the notebook manually. ANCHOR should provide an in-app launch and download page for the external solver notebooks and benchmark bundle.
acceptanceCriteria: Researcher Quick Start exposes the full notebook, starter notebook, public bundle, and finalizer command.
The app states that users do not need the full source repository for normal Alpha use.
The hosted Colab button is enabled only when a public GitHub notebook URL is configured.

items.title: Hosted Google Colab smoke pending
items.affectedWorkflow: External Solver Notebook / Google Colab
items.summary: Local Python notebook execution and authoritative ANCHOR finalization are verified, but a real hosted Google Colab Run All smoke remains pending.
items.decision: Track separately from local notebook verification.
acceptanceCriteria: Hosted Google Colab status remains PENDING until a real hosted run is completed.
Documentation distinguishes local Python verification from hosted Colab verification.
No release surface claims hosted Colab verification without evidence.

items.title: Feedback and diagnostic package taxonomy
items.affectedWorkflow: Alpha Feedback and Diagnostics
items.summary: Alpha feedback should be categorized consistently as P0/P1/P2/P3 and SCI, EDU, BENCH, OPS, UX, PERF, or ACCESS.
items.decision: Use feedback ledger as the source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Feedback IDs are stable and parseable.
Statuses and category tags are auditable.
P0/P1 items cannot be silently marked ignored.

items.title: Environment Studio needs regional 3D bathymetry authoring, not flat 2D tile swatches.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio
items.summary: Alpha review found that the R1 editor still appears like a flat 2D tile board and is too dominated by localized shore/shelf tiles. Users want to author larger mission-scale synthetic regions, including gulf-like basins, shelves, canyons, islands, seamounts, river-mouth zones, ridges, sills, and deep-water mission opportunities suitable for multiple gliders.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-STUDIO-R1.1 regional input model, 3D preview, contextual inspector, and multi-archetype regional generator controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio remains one unified editor under Simulation Lab.
Regional bathymetry authoring exposes 3D preview, source-grid versus preview-mesh metadata, and multi-archetype provenance.
The phase does not change simulation, scoring, current generation, scalar generation, benchmark fairness, or Product Hub pillars.

items.title: Environment Studio should start from a Synthetic Ocean Atlas and operational window selection.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio
items.summary: Alpha review found that mission authors think in terms of operational areas, not low-level terrain-feature controls. Environment Studio should present a simplified synthetic world/ocean atlas where users draw an operational window near coast, gulf, island, strait, shelf break, deep basin, river mouth, or open ocean regions. The selected window should infer a regional mission recipe that drives bathymetry, current/scalar regimes, mission scale, glider count, and validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a Synthetic Ocean Atlas stage before feature/tile tuning.
Operational window selection records detected regional context and mission recipe metadata.
Feature and source-tile controls remain available as advanced provenance after regional generation.

items.title: Synthetic Ocean Atlas needs a procedural field engine and window-conditioned bathymetry generator.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic Ocean Atlas
items.summary: The current atlas is too symbolic. Alpha review wants a seeded synthetic world map whose environmental fields determine land masses, coastline context, shelf/basin/island/gulf regimes, current/scalar regime hints, and generated regional bathymetry from a selected operational window.
acceptanceCriteria: Atlas generation is deterministic, procedural, field-based, and not a real Earth map.
Operational window inference samples atlas fields and produces a Regional Mission Recipe.
Generated bathymetry comes from structured procedural features, distance fields, seeded placement, controlled roughness, validation, and provenance.

items.title: Synthetic Ocean Atlas should regenerate package-backed current, scalar, and hotspot artifacts.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Field Regeneration
items.summary: After regional bathymetry generation, Environment Studio should be able to regenerate deterministic synthetic CurrentField4D, ScalarField4D, hotspot candidates, and field diagnostics from atlas context, bathymetry, masks, coastline, open boundaries, feature zones, and regime hints.
items.decision: Accepted for FIELD-REGEN-R1 as a package-backed synthetic regeneration pass. It does not launch missions from Studio projects, change simulation, change scoring, claim calibrated ocean products, or create operational forecasts.
acceptanceCriteria: Current regeneration uses packages/currents and a reduced-order bathymetry/atlas-conditioned synthetic backend.
Scalar and hotspot regeneration uses packages/scalar-processes when package adapters are available.
Generated metadata records digests, components, diagnostics, dependency states, and claim boundaries.
Starts/drop zones remain NEEDS_VALIDATION and benchmark bundles remain REQUIRES_REGENERATION.
No exported public artifact claims HYCOM, Marine Copernicus, calibrated ocean forecasts, operational forecasts, hidden truth, simulation changes, or scoring changes.

items.title: Environment Studio should be reauthored around a procedural synthetic world map and user-drawn operational boundary.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio
items.summary: Current Environment Studio remains too parameter-heavy and symbolic. Alpha review wants a generated high-resolution synthetic world map with land masses, islands, oceans, and coarse flow-regime context. Users should pan/zoom the world map, define their own operational boundary box, and then generate regional 3D bathymetry from that selected window.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a deterministic synthetic world-map artifact.
Users select an operational boundary window that samples world fields.
Selected windows drive regional 3D bathymetry generation while mission planning, scoring, current/scalar equations, and launch workflows remain unchanged.

items.title: Environment Studio must use a real pan/zoom procedural synthetic world map, not pixel-grid atlas art.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic World Map
items.summary: Alpha review found that the Environment Studio world map still appears as static pixel-grid art with a heavy control panel. Users want to generate a large synthetic Earth-like ocean world with land masses, islands, oceans, and coarse environmental fields; pan and zoom around it; select their own operational boundary; and then generate regional 3D bathymetry from that selected window.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a large generated synthetic world-map viewport rather than a symbolic atlas diagram.
Users can pan, zoom, choose broad generation controls, and drag an operational boundary window.
Selected windows sample deterministic synthetic world fields and drive regional 3D bathymetry generation without changing mission simulation, scoring, planners, or current/scalar equations.

items.title: Environment Studio needs hard visual acceptance for a world-map-first workflow.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic World Map
items.summary: Alpha review found that the Environment Studio world-map pass still risked reading like a symbolic local atlas or schematic tile board. The workflow needs a hard browser visual acceptance package proving that Stage 1 opens on a large procedural synthetic world map with pan/zoom, layers, a selected operational boundary, and regional bathymetry generated from that boundary.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-WORLD-R1A as a visual acceptance and workflow hardening pass. It does not change mission simulation, scoring, planner behavior, current/scalar generation equations, benchmark fairness, or existing Alpha workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio Stage 1 default is a Synthetic World Map viewport, not a symbolic atlas diagram or DOM cell grid.
Owner-review screenshots capture default, panned, zoomed, bathymetry-layer, flow-layer, selected-boundary, and generated-regional-bathymetry states.

The QA summary records world/window digests, pan/zoom evidence, visible land/island/open-ocean metrics, selected-window area, forbidden Stage 1 control count, hidden-truth status, and unchanged simulation/scoring flags.
The selected operational window remains a small regional subset of the synthetic world and drives regional 3D bathymetry generation.

items.title: Flat synthetic world-map UI rejected; Environment Studio needs high-resolution synthetic globe selector.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic Globe Selector
items.summary: Alpha review rejected the low-resolution local flat-map mental model. Environment Studio Stage 1 should generate a deterministic high-resolution equirectangular synthetic world-field artifact, render it as the primary interactive globe selector, let users select a small operational globe region, and generate regional 2.5D bathymetry from that selected context.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-GLOBE-R1 as a front-door reauthoring pass. The globe is the selector, the equirectangular fields are the canonical generated artifact, and regional bathymetry is the output. Currents, scalars, hotspots, launch-to-planning, simulation, scoring, planner behavior, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio Stage 1 default is a visible interactive globe, not a flat rectangle or pixel-grid map.
The first artifact is `anchor.synthetic-globe-world` with canonical equirectangular resolution at least 2048 x 1024 and default 4096 x 2048.
Users can rotate and zoom the globe, inspect synthetic layers, and select a small operational region below 5 percent of the globe.
Selected regions produce `anchor.operational-globe-window` context and can generate regional 3D bathymetry through the existing builder.
Owner-review screenshots and QA summary are written under `test-results/env-globe-r1-owner-review/`.

No exported public artifact claims real Earth, GEBCO, ETOPO, HYCOM, Copernicus, calibrated survey data, operational forecast, certified navigation, hidden truth, simulation changes, or scoring changes.

items.title: Environment Studio should start from a reference bathymetry atlas and user-selected real patch.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review clarified that the issue is not 2D versus globe; the active front door should be a reference bathymetry atlas with lon/lat bounding-box selection and regional patch extraction. Procedural world and globe workflows should be demoted to an experimental sandbox.
items.decision: Accepted for REAL-BATHY-R1 as a production-path correction. The workflow is reference bathymetry atlas -> bounding box -> extracted patch -> regional 3D bathymetry. If no preprocessed public GEBCO/ETOPO fixture is checked in, the browser must show an explicit NO_REFERENCE_DATA_FIXTURE placeholder and must not claim real-data completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio defaults to Reference Bathymetry Atlas, not procedural synthetic world or globe.
Users can pan/zoom the reference atlas, select a lon/lat bounding box, inspect selected patch metadata, and generate regional 3D bathymetry from the selected patch.
Procedural synthetic world/globe remains reachable only as an experimental sandbox or compatibility path.
Owner-review screenshots and QA summary are written under `test-results/real-bathy-r1-owner-review/`.
Exports preserve reference dataset identity, atlas digest, selected patch digest, bathymetry artifact digest, validation status, and deferred current/scalar/hotspot dependencies.
If no public reference fixture exists, artifacts and docs clearly report `REAL_BATHY_R1_BLOCKED_WAITING_FOR_REFERENCE_FIXTURE` and `NO_REFERENCE_DATA_FIXTURE`.
Mission simulation, official scoring, planners, glider dynamics, current/scalar generation, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.

items.title: Reference bathymetry patch needs coupled environment field generation.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Field Generation
items.summary: ANCHOR now has a verified 15 arc-second Monterey Canyon reference bathymetry patch. To become a usable mission environment, Environment Studio must generate bathymetry-conditioned synthetic currents, scalar fields, hotspots, candidate starts/drop zones, hazards, and an EnvironmentArtifact from that reference patch.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference bathymetry generates deterministic synthetic current, scalar, hotspot, start/drop-zone, and hazard metadata.
Exports preserve reference fixture identity, field digests, dependency states, validation report, provenance, and claim boundaries.
Currents and scalars are labeled as synthetic bathymetry-conditioned benchmark fields, not operational forecasts.
Mission simulation, scoring, planners, glider dynamics, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.

items.title: Reference-derived generated environments need composition, launch validation, and benchmark export.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Planning Launch / Benchmark Export
items.summary: Environment Studio can now generate reference-derived bathymetry and synthetic bathymetry-conditioned fields, but generated projects still stop before package-backed EnvironmentArtifact composition, validated launch to Planning, and public benchmark-bundle export. Users need the generated environment to become a playable and benchmarkable mission scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference-derived field outputs compose into a package-backed EnvironmentArtifact or block with a named contract gap.
Launch validation promotes valid start/drop-zone candidates before Planning launch.
Mission Workspace opens the generated reference-derived environment while retaining route-planning ownership.
Public benchmark bundle export includes reference environment digests and excludes hidden truth, raw external_data paths, operational forecast claims, simulation changes, and scoring changes.

items.title: Reference-derived environment workflow needs launch-warning closure and owner acceptance package.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Environment Launch Acceptance
items.summary: The reference-derived Monterey Canyon environment can now compose, validate, launch to Planning, and export benchmark bundles. Before returning to alpha testers, the launch WARN state needs explicit taxonomy, owner-visible screenshots, public-safety proof, and a complete acceptance package showing the workflow from Environment Studio to Planning and benchmark export.
acceptanceCriteria: Launch warnings are classified as INFO, ADVISORY, NON_BLOCKING_WARN, BLOCKING_WARN, or FAIL.
Planning launch is ready only when no blocking warnings or failures are present.
Owner-review screenshots and QA summary prove Environment Studio composition, launch validation, Planning, execution, Debrief, project roundtrip, and benchmark export.
Public artifacts remain free of hidden truth and raw external_data paths.
Mission simulation, scoring, planners, glider dynamics, and field equations remain unchanged.

items.title: Run alpha retest on reference-derived Monterey Canyon workflow.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Environment Alpha Retest
items.summary: The reference-derived Monterey Canyon workflow now composes, validates, launches to Planning, executes missions, reaches Debrief, and exports public benchmark bundles. Human alpha retest is required before adding variants, dataset factories, or additional environment authoring features.
acceptanceCriteria: Stable owner-review evidence is available from an ignored local artifact path.
Human testers have a concise task script for Environment Studio through Planning, execution, Debrief, and benchmark export.
Feedback intake captures provenance clarity, claim-boundary clarity, warning clarity, usability, scientific concerns, education concerns, and benchmark concerns.
The retest handoff preserves the deterministic benchmark claim boundary and does not change simulation, scoring, planners, glider dynamics, or field equations.

items.title: Reference atlas should open as a global selector before regional patch generation.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that Environment Studio still read like a local Monterey patch viewer. The production path should open on a global reference overview, show staged patch coverage, require loading a staged regional fixture before generation, and export a patch request when a selected region is not staged.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio defaults to Global Atlas Selector, not a regional Monterey patch workspace.
Manifest metadata distinguishes global overview, mission-ready patch, and low-resolution fallback roles.
Available patch coverage is visible and selectable before regional generation.
Unstaged regions produce a patch-request artifact instead of placeholder reference bathymetry.
The owner-review package records overview, patch coverage, staged patch load, generated environment, hidden-truth exclusion, raw-path exclusion, and unchanged simulation/scoring flags.

items.title: Reference atlas should allow large operational windows without pretending they are live browser patches.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that large Gulf-scale selections were still treated like one browser-generated patch. Environment Studio now separates the selected OperationalWindow from the GenerationBudget, keeps large valid windows selectable, disables live generation for multi-tile regions, and exports an explicit multi-tile patch request artifact for offline preprocessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Local, regional, fleet, Gulf segment, and basin campaign presets are selectable as operational windows.
Gulf-scale windows report MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED, generationAllowed=false, patchRequestAllowed=true, multiTileRecommended=true, and recommendedAction=exportMultiTilePatchRequest.
Tiny click-only selections expand or normalize to a usable local operational window.
The multi-tile patch request artifact preserves source dataset identity, resolution, tile plan, suggested tile bounds, commands, claim boundary, and digest without raw local paths or hidden truth.
The Monterey mission-ready patch still loads, generates bathymetry and fields, composes an environment, and validates launch readiness.

items.title: Reference atlas needs deep zoom and direct operational-window editing.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that the atlas could select large regions but still lacked enough close zoom and an obvious operational-window editor for center, size, and lon/lat bounds. Environment Studio now supports deep atlas zoom, visible typed operational-window editing, tiny-selection guidance, local/regional/fleet single patch requests, Gulf/basin multi-tile patch requests, and Monterey patch continuity evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: The atlas can zoom to at least 16x and reset to the full world view.
Operational windows can be edited by mode, center lon/lat, size in kilometers, and west/east/south/north bounds.
Tiny click or drag selections show mission-planning guidance and expand to a useful local or regional window.
Local, regional, and fleet survey windows export single patch requests, while Gulf and basin windows export multi-tile patch requests.
The Monterey mission-ready patch still focuses, loads, generates bathymetry and fields, composes an environment, and validates launch readiness without changing simulation or scoring.

items.title: Create scripted static ETOPO tile pipeline for app-hosted reference bathymetry.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: ANCHOR should not depend on live NOAA/GEBCO downloads during browser runtime. The app needs a scripted offline pipeline that downloads selected ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second source tiles, crops/validates them, generates app-ready raster and mesh LOD artifacts, and registers them in an app-hosted static tile library.
acceptanceCriteria: Raw ETOPO source tiles are resolved and downloaded by script for selected regions, not by browser runtime.
Raw source data remains ignored under external_data/reference_bathymetry/.
App-ready raster and non-authoritative mesh LOD artifacts are generated under assets/reference_bathymetry/.
The tile-library manifest registers staged Monterey tile sets and request-only Gulf coverage honestly.
Environment Studio loads staged ANCHOR static tile assets without NOAA/GEBCO runtime fetches, raw local paths, or hidden truth exposure.

items.title: Run alpha retest on app-hosted static reference tile library workflow.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Static Reference Tile Library
items.summary: The static tile library pipeline is implemented. Human alpha retest should verify that users understand hosted staged bathymetry tiles, non-authoritative mesh LOD previews, raster/grid authority, Monterey mission-ready loading, and Gulf requestOnly/multi-tile export behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner-review evidence proves the browser loads hosted reference bathymetry tile-library assets without NOAA/GEBCO runtime fetches.
Monterey 15 arc-second remains the mission-ready hosted tile set and exposes non-authoritative mesh LOD previews.
Raster/grid bathymetry remains the authoritative input for bathymetry sampling and environment generation.
Gulf-scale regions remain requestOnly and export multi-tile patch requests instead of pretending staged Gulf assets exist.

The retest protocol and feedback template ask testers about hosted tiles, mesh authority, raster authority, Monterey loading, Gulf requestOnly behavior, multi-tile request clarity, and Planning mission completion.

items.title: Atlas operational-window rectangle needs direct move and resize handles.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Global Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review shows that users cannot easily control the selected atlas boundary box. The operational window must support standard rectangle-editing interactions: drag inside to move, drag edges to resize one side, drag corners to resize both sides, plus numeric bounds/size updates and budget refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: The atlas selected operational window can be moved by dragging inside the rectangle.
Edges resize one side while preserving the opposite edge and corners resize both connected sides.
Rectangle edits synchronize numeric lon/lat and size controls, boundary budget, and patch availability.
Large operational windows remain valid selections but live Alpha generation remains budget-gated.
Monterey 15 arc-second still loads, and Gulf-scale selections still export multi-tile patch requests without changing simulation, scoring, planners, or field equations.

items.title: Environment Studio needs a distinct atlas staging scene and local bathymetry scene.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review clarified the desired Environment Studio workflow. The global atlas should be a staging/setup scene for selecting an operational boundary window. Once a staged hosted tile exists for that boundary, the user should continue into a local/regional 3D bathymetry scene defined by the selected bounds. Unstaged regions should route to patch-request workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a Global Atlas Setup Scene with tools/actions on the left, atlas map in the center, and selected-region inspector on the right.
Continue to Mission-Ready Bathymetry is enabled only for hosted mission-ready tile selections.
Continue opens RegionalBathymetryScene with selected bounds, tile set metadata, raster digest, and non-authoritative mesh LOD metadata.
Unstaged regions export patch requests, and Gulf-scale regions export multi-tile patch requests without scene transition.
Raster/grid bathymetry remains authoritative, mesh LODs remain visualization-only, and browser runtime does not fetch NOAA/GEBCO or expose raw external_data paths.

items.title: Atlas staging action buttons show enabled state for request-only regions.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Global Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that a Gulf-scale notStaged / MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED operational window still shows green Continue to Mission-Ready Bathymetry and Load Mission Patch buttons. Clicking Continue silently does nothing. The UI should disable or hide unsupported launch actions and make Export Multi-Tile Request the primary action.
acceptanceCriteria: Continue to Mission-Ready Bathymetry is disabled and visually grey for no selection, notStaged selections, and MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED selections.
Load Mission Patch is disabled for notStaged and Gulf-scale request-only selections.
Export Patch Request is the primary request action for local or regional notStaged selections.
Export Multi-Tile Request is the primary request action for Gulf-scale or basin-scale MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED selections.
Monterey 15 arc-second mission-ready selection keeps Continue to Mission-Ready Bathymetry enabled and opens RegionalBathymetryScene.
Unsupported actions do not silently no-op and record visible blocked-action feedback without changing simulation, scoring, planners, or field equations.

items.title: Large valid Gulf-scale operational areas need an inspectable path before offline staging.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Global Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that a valid Gulf-scale operational area felt blocked when the only visible path was MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED and request export. Large selections should feel usable without pretending the browser can generate a giant mission-ready patch.
acceptanceCriteria: Large Gulf-style regions remain valid operational areas with operationalSelectionStatus=VALID and generationBudgetStatus=MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED.
Open 3D Bathymetry Preview is enabled for valid selected regions, including request-only and MULTI_TILE_REQUIRED regions.
Coarse preview clearly states that it is not mission-ready, not suitable for official simulation/scoring, and requires staged multi-tile bathymetry before Planning launch.
Generate Fields, Compose Environment, Launch Planning, and benchmark export stay disabled from coarse preview.
Gulf-scale request-only regions still export multi-tile patch requests, and Monterey 15 arc-second still opens as the mission-ready single-tile path.
No browser NOAA/GEBCO fetch, raw external_data path, hidden truth, simulation change, scoring change, planner change, or field-equation change is introduced.

items.title: Any valid operational boundary should open a bathymetry representation.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Global Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review found that Environment Studio still feels broken when a user draws a valid not-staged boundary and sees no bathymetry representation. The product rule is that every valid operational boundary can open a preview; mission-ready generation remains gated on staged app-hosted tiles.
acceptanceCriteria: Every valid boundary can open an interactive 3D bathymetry preview.
If no app-hosted mission-ready bathymetry tile is staged, the preview uses the coarse global overview and is not mission-ready.
Field generation, Planning launch, and benchmark export remain disabled until high-resolution app-hosted bathymetry tiles are staged and validated.
Valid notStaged regional boxes and large Gulf boxes open coarsePreview mode.
Monterey mission-ready selection opens stagedSingleTile mode through Open 3D Bathymetry Preview or Continue to Mission-Ready Bathymetry.
No browser NOAA/GEBCO fetch, raw external_data path, hidden truth, simulation change, scoring change, planner change, or field-equation change is introduced.

items.title: Environment Studio needs simplified atlas controls and real 3D bathymetry previews.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Global Reference Bathymetry Atlas / Regional 3D Bathymetry Workspace
items.summary: Alpha review found that the atlas left panel remained too diagnostic-heavy and the coarse preview felt like a placeholder instead of a bathymetry scene. Every valid boundary should open an interactive 3D bathymetry preview with adaptive LOD while mission-ready generation stays gated on staged tiles.
acceptanceCriteria: The default atlas left panel shows only header, atlas tools, window presets, boundary actions, and collapsed Advanced controls.
The right panel owns selected operational-window bounds, bathymetry availability, scale, budget, and next-step status.
Every valid boundary can open Open 3D Bathymetry Preview.
Large Gulf-scale regions remain valid and open an adaptive-LOD interactive 3D preview under browser mesh caps.
Coarse previews keep field generation, Planning launch, and benchmark export disabled until staged mission-ready tiles exist.
Monterey 15 arc-second mission-ready selection still opens stagedSingleTile mode and preserves the field-generation path.
No browser NOAA/GEBCO fetch, raw external_data path, hidden truth, simulation change, scoring change, planner change, or field-equation change is introduced.
